I'm a Toronto-based data researcher with a
Master's in cognitive neuroscience, two peer-reviewed publications,
and a public-service role at Statistics Canada.

R is my native analytical language. I’m also using Oracle SQL, APEX, and Python
to build BonQuery's projects end to end: database, dashboard, analysis, and
writing.

I started BonQuery because so much of the publicly available data
on humanitarian issues in Canada sits on government open-data pages
where most people will never see it. The first project focuses on
Toronto's taxed shelter system. More to follow.

## Language: homeless, unhoused, and people experiencing homelessness

People use **homeless**, **unhoused**, and **people experiencing homelessness**.
Some people and activists prefer **unhoused** because it names the lack of
housing, not a fixed identity. Others use **homeless** for themselves and for
established research, services, and advocacy. No single term speaks for
everyone.

BonQuery usually says **people experiencing homelessness** or **people without
housing**. We use **homeless** when it is part of an official name, a direct
quote, a research title, or a search term people use to find this work. We do
not call people “the homeless.” We will keep listening to people with lived
experience and change our wording when needed.

**Needing shelter is not the same as being homeless.** Someone may still have an
address but be unable to return safely. Adults, children, and families fleeing
violence may need an emergency shelter or a warm place without being homeless.

**Housing insecure** is broader than **unhoused**. It includes people whose
housing is unsafe, unstable, unaffordable, or about to be lost. That can include
someone staying temporarily with other people or fleeing violence. A person can
be housing insecure without appearing in the City shelter data at all. We use
this term only when we mean that wider group.

This approach follows [person-first language guidance](https://nhchc.org/research/publications/trauma-informed-organizations-change-package/strengths-based/){target="_blank"}
and research on [why housing is central to the meaning of
homelessness](https://www.homelesshub.ca/sites/default/files/attachments/Intro_Hulchanski_et_al_-_Homelessness_Word.pdf){target="_blank"}.
It also follows the [Canadian definition of
homelessness](https://homelesshub.ca/book/pandemic-preparedness-and-homelessness-lessons-from-h1n1-in-canada/appendix-a-canadian-definition-of-homelessness/){target="_blank"}
and recognizes the established name of York University's [Canadian
Observatory on Homelessness](https://yorkspace.library.yorku.ca/communities/081a5bc9-a172-4b31-a371-60715b0130c7){target="_blank"}.

## Open methods and public code

The [BonQuery.ca repository](https://github.com/MiriamMarling/bonquery.ca){target="_blank"}
is public. It contains the Quarto pages, styles, publishing workflows, and
aggregated data used by the website. The raw-data pipelines and primary research
analysis remain in a separate private repository while manuscript work is
underway.

If you find a problem in the website or its published data, you can
[open an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/MiriamMarling/bonquery.ca/issues){target="_blank"}.
